re_line: Trump threatens tax on offshore AI data centres · Australia-China agree annual AI dialogue · Cyclone Xavier weakens, Cook Islands relief sails · Fiji reopens Brussels embassy · NZD at post-GFC low
morning_memo: Trump vowed a "tremendous tax" on American companies building data centres abroad, putting Microsoft's $25 billion and Amazon's $20 billion Australian commitments in question.
Canberra and Beijing agreed to annual artificial intelligence talks and deeper climate cooperation, capping a week in which Xi Jinping declared a "full turnaround" in the relationship.

Cook Islands Prime Minister Mark Brown loaded relief supplies onto the Kukupa for the Northern group after Tropical Cyclone Xavier weakened to category 1, with a New Zealand Air Force C-130 delivering humanitarian cargo to Rarotonga.

top_stories.headline: Trump vows 'tremendous tax' on US companies building data centres offshore
top_stories.body: **Donald Trump** said he would impose a "tremendous tax" on American companies that build data centres outside the United States. "We're not allowing data centres to go into other countries," he told a White House briefing, framing the move as part of the artificial intelligence contest with China. Microsoft announced a *$25 billion* Australian data centre investment in April and Amazon a $20 billion plan in June. Trump also talked down the Quad artificial intelligence agreement with Australia, India, and Japan: "It's wonderful to say we're working with other countries to build, but I want it in this country."
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News: "Trump vows 'tremendous tax' on companies building data centres abroad" · also SMH

top_stories.headline: Australia and China agree to annual AI talks and deeper climate cooperation
top_stories.body: Australia and China agreed to hold annual artificial intelligence talks to manage the risks of the technology, alongside a commitment to deepen cooperation on climate change. The agreement closes a week of summitry in which **Anthony Albanese** attended APEC in Shenzhen and **Xi Jinping** hailed a "full turnaround" in bilateral relations. The ABC's Stephen Dziedzic reported from Beijing that deep differences between the two governments remain.
top_stories.src_line: per Sydney Morning Herald: "Australia and China agree to annual AI talks to manage risks" · also ABC News

top_stories.headline: Cook Islands moves relief to Northern group as Cyclone Xavier weakens
top_stories.body: **Mark Brown** declared a state of emergency for Nassau Island ahead of Tropical Cyclone Xavier, now downgraded to category 1. A New Zealand Air Force C-130 was due in Rarotonga with humanitarian supplies for loading onto the Kukupa, which is carrying generator parts for Rakahanga. The barge Taunga Nui is fully loaded for Pukapuka and Nassau and will depart after the weekend once conditions allow. Pukapuka lost its traditional wale pola, a landmark that had stood for decades.
top_stories.src_line: per RNZ Pacific: "Cook Islands PM says relief supplies on standby as TC Xavier weakens" · also Cook Islands News

overnight_items.headline: Trump, Xi, and Putin issue 'declaration of peace' after 90 minutes in Shenzhen
overnight_items.body_text: The three presidents met for the first time together at Kylin Villa on November 19 on the sidelines of APEC, with nuclear disarmament, Ukraine, and the war in Iran on the agenda. After 90 minutes they released a joint "declaration of peace" pledging reform of the United Nations. The ABC's assessment was that few deliverables emerged from the meeting.

overnight_items.headline: Albanese raises Ukraine directly with Putin at the close of an 11-day trip
overnight_items.body_text: Anthony Albanese spent 11 days visiting three countries, battling illness, and faced criticism for standing alongside **Vladimir Putin** in the APEC family photo in Shenzhen. The prime minister had said for days he would not miss the chance to tell Putin what he thought of the war in Ukraine. Tom McIlroy writes that his flourish-free, middle-power approach guided the performance.

overnight_items.headline: Fiji reopens Brussels embassy after nearly five decades of EU engagement
overnight_items.body_text: Minister for Foreign Affairs and External Trade **Sakiasi Ditoka** inaugurated the embassy on November 20 on behalf of Prime Minister **Sitiveni Rabuka**. Ditoka pointed to the Samoa Agreement and the Interim Economic Partnership Agreement as the frame for the relationship. Fiji first established a diplomatic presence in Brussels in July 1973; the reopened post also covers Belgium, European institutions, and the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States.

overnight_items.headline: New Zealand dollar hits its lowest level since the global financial crisis
overnight_items.body_text: Bloomberg reported the New Zealand dollar fell to its weakest level since the global financial crisis. The pre-collected market data has NZD/USD at *0.5470*, down 1.05 percent as of November 21, with the NZX 50 at 14,107, down 0.47 percent as of November 20. The Australian dollar sat at 0.6619, down 2.36 percent.

overnight_items.headline: Australia's jobless rate rises to its highest level since 2021
overnight_items.body_text: The Wall Street Journal reported Australia's unemployment rate climbed to its highest since 2021. The figure lands with the ASX 200 at 8,593, down 5.39 percent as of November 20, and the Australian dollar at 0.6619. The RBA held the cash rate at 4.35 percent on 11 August 2026, a second consecutive hold after three increases earlier in the year.

overnight_items.headline: Marape and Marcos discuss trade, investment, and food security on APEC margins
overnight_items.body_text: Prime Minister **James Marape** held bilateral talks with Philippines President **Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr** on November 19 on the sidelines of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen. The two discussed strengthening relations and expanding trade and investment between Papua New Guinea and the Philippines. Marape separately thanked world leaders for recognising Papua New Guinea's voice at the meeting.

pacific_wire.headline: Vanuatu and China sign agreement for 3,000 solar streetlights at COP31
pacific_wire.body_text: Vanuatu and China signed an agreement at COP31 covering *3,000 solar streetlights*. The deal was struck on the margins of the climate conference in Antalya, where Vanuatu's delegation also launched its National Adaptation Plan 2026-2035.

pacific_wire.headline: Vanuatu says all six of its research positions made the agreed COP31 text
pacific_wire.body_text: Vanuatu's delegation secured all six of its positions on research and systematic observation in the agreed text, including references to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, the 1.5C limit, and traditional knowledge. Four Alliance of Small Island States priorities were included in the text on the Warsaw International Mechanism for Loss and Damage and the Santiago Network. The National Adaptation Plan 2026-2035 was launched on 13 November at the Moana Blue Pacific Pavilion.

pacific_wire.headline: Australia adds $10 million to Pacific-led ocean initiative at COP31
pacific_wire.body_text: **Chris Bowen**, Australia's Climate Change and Energy Minister and COP31 President of Negotiations, announced an additional *$10 million* for the Pacific-led Unlocking Blue Prosperity Initiative, plus AUD$1 million over two years for the Ocean Risk and Resilience Action Alliance. Fiji's Minister for Environment and Climate Change **Lynda Tabuya** welcomed the commitments but called for simpler, more direct access to funding for women, young people, and small-scale fishers.

pacific_wire.headline: Samoan prime minister visits American Samoa weeks after Atoa o Samoa talks lapse
pacific_wire.body_text: Prime Minister **La'aulialemalietoa Leuatea Schmidt** travelled to American Samoa on Saturday morning and was welcomed by Governor **Pulaali'i Nikolao Pula**. The visit follows the failure of the latest round of Atoa o Samoa talks to take place as scheduled. He was accompanied by the chairman of the Samoa Rugby Union.

pacific_wire.headline: Cook Islands High Court weighs recount over 13 votes in Matavera petition
pacific_wire.body_text: Justice **Christine Grice** reserved her decision on the Matavera electoral petition, indicating she hopes to rule by next Friday. The court must decide whether a recount is necessary, with 13 votes under scrutiny.

pacific_wire.headline: Vanuatu sends Fiji a draft air services agreement for Santo-Nadi flights
pacific_wire.body_text: Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and External Trade **Marc Ati** confirmed a draft air services agreement for direct flights between Pekoa Airport in Santo and Nadi has gone to Fijian authorities. The Council of Ministers approved the route last month under COM Decision No. 377, cleared by the Office of the Attorney General and the Civil Aviation Authority. Ati estimated the service could provide between 900 and 2,000 seats a week, and said New Caledonia talks on Pekoa-Tontouta flights would follow.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji rejected 6,000 work permit applications over fraudulent documents
pacific_wire.body_text: Immigration Minister **Viliame Naupoto** said the department rejected *6,000 work permit applications* between August 2024 and November 2025 because of fraudulent documents. The department received 39,000 permit applications in the period, of which 21,000 were work permits and 15,000 were approved. Naupoto linked the fraud to human trafficking and migrant smuggling riding on Fiji's role as a regional travel hub, with 986,000 visitors and 300,000 transit passengers.

pacific_wire.headline: Cyclone Xavier weakens to category 1, direct impact on Samoa assessed as low
pacific_wire.body_text: The Samoa Meteorological Service said Xavier had weakened rapidly to category 2 by 1am and was downgraded to category 1 by 7am, sitting about 920 kilometres northeast of Apia. A wind advisory and marine warning remain in effect nationwide. Xavier reached category 5 on Wednesday after first being identified as a tropical disturbance on November 13.

pacific_wire.headline: Kamikamica says a reintroduced Senate would give traditional leadership a voice
pacific_wire.body_text: Deputy Prime Minister **Manoa Kamikamica** told the Fijian Media Association's Town Hall in Nadi that the proposed reintroduction of a Senate aims to promote national unity and ensure traditional leadership has a voice in governance. NextGEN Alliance President **Vishal Goundar** raised the question at the event.

new_zealand.headline: O'Sullivan: New Zealand cannot afford to be squeezed between Washington and Beijing
new_zealand.body_text: Fran O'Sullivan argues from the APEC summit that New Zealand cannot afford to be caught between the United States and China. The piece lands as the New Zealand dollar trades at its weakest since the global financial crisis.

new_zealand.headline: New Zealander jailed in Australia over explosive-making instructions and extremist material
new_zealand.body_text: An Australian court jailed a New Zealander found with instructions for making explosives and extremist material, RNZ reported.

canberra_politics.headline: Hartcher: refusing to help the US on Iran would once have been an alliance breach
canberra_politics.body_text: Peter Hartcher writes that in Canberra convention, refusal to help America in its war on Iran is tantamount to a breach of the alliance, and argues Anthony Albanese has done it and got away with it.

canberra_politics.headline: Proposed change would let Australians sue big tech under the digital duty of care
canberra_politics.body_text: Australians could sue big technology companies under a proposed change to the government's digital duty of care law. The amendment follows the government conceding to the Greens this week to pass its right-to-sue social media bill.

canberra_politics.headline: Canberra vows to manage AI agent shoppers and surveillance pricing
canberra_politics.body_text: Australia said the law must keep pace with artificial intelligence shopping agents and surveillance pricing, Bloomberg reported. The commitment sits alongside the digital duty of care changes and the new Australia-China artificial intelligence dialogue.

canberra_politics.headline: Bowen's COP31 deal in doubt as an activist derails a session in Antalya
canberra_politics.body_text: Chris Bowen is under pressure to deliver a binding resolution at COP31 in Turkiye as negotiations spill into overtime, with a climate activist derailing one session. Bowen holds the COP31 Presidency of Negotiations.

canberra_politics.headline: Rallies in 26 locations oppose the January scrapping of the midwife insurance exemption
canberra_politics.body_text: Homebirth Australia organised rallies at *26 locations* against the removal from January 1 of a longstanding exemption allowing privately practising midwives to attend homebirths without indemnity insurance. About 5 percent of Australia's 35,000 registered midwives are endorsed and able to obtain the insurance, according to AHPRA Nursing and Midwifery Board data.

business_economy.headline: Westpac injects $225 million into its Fiji subsidiary
business_economy.body_text: Westpac Group will invest *$225 million* in Westpac Fiji to expand lending capacity and strengthen its balance sheet. Westpac chief executive, business and wealth, **Paul Fowler** said Fiji is "a key economic partner for Australia" and cited the Vuvale Union Treaty as bringing the two countries closer. The bank marks 125 years of operating in Fiji this year.

business_economy.headline: Fiji's hydro dams could shut by end of January as El Nino drought bites
business_economy.body_text: Energy Fiji Limited warned on November 20 that the Monasavu and Nadarivatu dams could be forced to shut for safety reasons by the end of January 2027. Hydroelectricity has fallen from 40 percent of generation a year ago to *30 percent*, with thermal rising to 70 percent as global fuel prices climb.

business_economy.headline: Fiji public service union seeks protections under the $20 million drought response
business_economy.body_text: The Fiji Public Service Association welcomed the government's *$20 million* emergency drought allocation but said it does not address the welfare and working conditions of staff implementing it. General secretary **Judith Kotobalavu** cited health, water, agriculture, and local government workers facing extreme heat and water shortages. The prime minister has declared a National State of Disaster.

primary_documents.headline: Wong interviewed on ABC News Breakfast
primary_documents.body_text: The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade published a transcript of **Penny Wong**'s interview with James Glenday on ABC News Breakfast.

calendar_watch.event: Cook Islands High Court decision on the Matavera electoral petition
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Justice Grice indicated she hopes to rule by next Friday on whether a recount of 13 votes is required.
Bowen, as President of Negotiations, is under pressure to land a binding resolution as talks run into overtime.
Only about 5 percent of Australia's 35,000 registered midwives will be able to attend homebirths.

calendar_watch.event: Energy Fiji Limited's projected shutdown point for the Monasavu and Nadarivatu dams
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: A shutdown would push Fiji further onto imported fuel for electricity amid the El Nino drought.

calendar_watch.event: Next mention in the Fiji Sports Council defamation case
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: A trial date is expected to be set after submissions close on the striking-out application.

key_stat.label: Microsoft's announced Australian data centre investment
key_stat.context: Trump's threatened tax on offshore data centres puts commitments of this scale, plus Amazon's $20 billion, under question.

also_today.headline: From Nadi to Babaka: turning climate commitments into action
also_today.body_text: Dianne Parascos, co-founder of the Papua New Guinean youth initiative Voices of the Soil, reports from Nadi on the gap between global climate finance commitments and the realities facing frontline communities.

also_today.headline: CSIS analysis: the Cook Islands and the future of seabed mining in the Pacific
also_today.body_text: CSIS published an analysis of the Cook Islands and the future of seabed mining in the Pacific.

also_today.headline: Fiji Immigration plans intelligence-led screening to detect trafficking at the border
also_today.body_text: Director of Immigration **Amelia Komaisavai** said a proposed trafficking-sensitive border management model would use Advance Passenger Information and Passenger Name Record data to flag high-risk travellers. She warned artificial intelligence is making forged documents almost indistinguishable from genuine ones.

also_today.headline: Prasad says the NFP will not back the third reading of Fiji's Constitution Amendment Bill
also_today.body_text: National Federation Party leader **Biman Prasad** said most Fijians have lost trust in the process behind the Constitution Amendment Bill 2026 and that the party identified 18 issues in the Cabinet subcommittee's draft, including errors and a proposal to recognise Christianity as a founding value. He said the process should be left until after the next general election.

also_today.headline: New Zealand to fund Vanuatu's Feiawa Park seafront stage redevelopment in 2027
also_today.body_text: New Zealand will fund the redevelopment of the Feiawa Park seafront stage in Vanuatu in 2027, the Daily Post reported.

also_today.headline: Vanuatu-Australia partnership strengthens police support for victims
also_today.body_text: A Vanuatu-Australia partnership is strengthening police support for victims, the Daily Post reported.

also_today.headline: Rio Tinto to contribute $370 million on Panguna mine impacts
also_today.body_text: ABC Pacific reported Rio Tinto will contribute *$370 million* to address the environmental and social impacts of the Panguna mine in Bougainville. The same programme covered Papua New Guinea's proposed three-child family policy and the twentieth anniversary of the Nuku'alofa pro-democracy riots.

opeds_today.headline: Albanese's filler in Manila
opeds_today.central_argument: Senior Labor ministers were anxious about Trump's late embrace of summitry, and success for Albanese is measured by avoiding recrimination rather than by outcomes.
opeds_today.summary: The piece reports that Albanese's colleagues were nervous about Donald Trump taking international summits seriously halfway through his second term. Trump's attendance at meetings in the Philippines and China created rare direct access for the prime minister. The article notes Joe Biden was the last president to convene the Quad, and that Trump has pivoted to foreign relations after the Republican loss of congressional control.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Sets expectations for what Canberra can extract from a reconvened Quad.

opeds_today.headline: By prodding Taiwan, Russia takes its alignment with China to new heights
opeds_today.central_argument: Russia is growing bolder in the Western Pacific and Australia and its partners should prepare for the implications.
opeds_today.summary: On 17 November two Russian bombers carried out an East Asian excursion. The Strategist frames the flight as evidence of deepening Russia-China alignment in the grey zone.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Adds a Russian vector to Australian planning assumptions about Western Pacific contingencies.
